The Old Bank on the River

The old bank stood beside the river for almost two hundred years. Its stone walls had survived floods, fires and several changes of ownership, and the townspeople regarded it with quiet affection.

When the council finally voted to close the building, an unexpected thing happened: neighbours began to gather on the steps each evening, trading stories about the people who had worked there.

A cartographer named Ingrid Halvorsen offered to draw a detailed map of the building before it was demolished. She worked for three weeks, recording every window, doorway and crack in the plaster.

Her drawing now hangs in the town library, a reminder that a place can outlast its purpose as long as someone takes the time to remember it carefully.

Extra paragraph so the page can scroll: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while the river keeps moving past the empty steps of the old building.

Another paragraph, because long-form pages are exactly where toolbar placement tends to break when the reader scrolls with a selection still active.

Final paragraph: the mill upstream still grinds flour on Saturdays, and its owner says the bank's old vault door would make a fine bread oven.
